newsitem.title: USA: Consumer prices post moderate increase in November.
newsitem.headline: Consumer prices post moderate increase in November.

text.p: Consumer prices advanced moderately in November, the government said on Thursday, in another sign of relative calm on the inflation front.
The Labor Department said the Consumer Price Index rose 0.3 percent, after rising by the same amount in October. Smaller increases in food prices helped to offset a surge in energy costs.
Excluding the typically volatile food and energy sectors, the "core" rate of inflation rose 0.2 percent after rising by an identical amount in October.
Both the overall index and the core rate matched Wall Street's forecasts.
The department said energy prices jumped 1.2 percent after jumping 0.7 percent in October. Gasoline prices rose 1.8 percent after gaining 0.7 percent in the month before.
Natural gas prices soared 3.4 percent in November, the biggest monthly gain since October 1982, when they were up 4.7 percent, the department said.
Food prices increased 0.3 percent after rising 0.6 in October.
New vehicle prices fell 0.1 percent in November after falling 0.2 percent in October. Airline fares fell 0.7 percent, while overall transportation prices rose 0.2 percent.
Housing prices advanced 0.2 percent after being up 0.3 percent in October. Medical care costs were up 0.3 percent after rising 0.2 percent in October.

In another report, the department said the number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell by 13,000 to 317,000 in the week ended December 7. Economists on average had expected claims to rise to 341,000.
The four-week moving average, a more accurate gauge of employment trends, also fell, dropping by 3,000 to 332,000.
